properties.areaDesc: Canadian; Oklahoma; Grady; McClain; Cleveland; Garvin
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 14 at 9:54PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 954 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 5 miles west of Yukon to 5 miles southwest of
Tabler to 4 miles north of Marlow. Movement was east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Western Oklahoma City, western Norman, Moore, El Reno, Chickasha,
Newcastle, Blanchard, Yukon, Bethany, Mustang, Warr Acres, The
Village, Tuttle, Piedmont, Nichols Hills, Lindsay, Union City, Minco,
Rush Springs, and Dibble.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

NWSheadline: Strong thunderstorms will impact portions of northwestern Garvin, Grady, western Oklahoma, northwestern Cleveland, southeastern Canadian and western McClain Counties through 1030 PM CDT

properties.areaDesc: Hall; Childress; Motley; Cottle; Dickens; King; Kent; Stonewall
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 9:50PM CDT until October 15 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of the Rolling Plains and the Panhandle of Texas,
including the following counties, Childress, Cottle, Dickens, Hall,
Kent, King, Motley and Stonewall.

* WHEN...Through 12 PM on Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Significant amounts of rain have fallen over the past 24 hours,
with totals already exceeding 5 inches in spots. An additional
round of heavy showers and thunderstorms is expected overnight
through Thursday morning, which may result in additional flooding
and/or the continuation of flooding which is already ongoing.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH NOON ON THURSDAY
